newsitem.title: CHINA: China savings seen at $456.6 billion end-October.
newsitem.headline: China savings seen at $456.6 billion end-October.

text.p: China's personal savings swelled to an estimated 3.79 trillion yuan ($456.6 billion) at the end of October, the China Daily Business Weekly said on Sunday.

The growth rate in personal savings was still high despite interest rate cuts in May and August, the newspaper quoted senior researcher with the State Council Development Research Centre Mi Jianguo as saying.
"Growth in savings suffered only a marginal setback: average year-on-year growth is still above 30 percent so far this year," the newspaper said.
An immature securities market and lack of other investment opportunities had meant many Chinese were still putting their money into savings accounts, Mi said.
Personal savings deposits had hit 3.67 trillion yuan ($442 billion) at the end of August, up 36.8 percent compared with the year before, he said.
That increase was 3.7 percentage points lower than the rise just before the first rate cut in May, Mi said.

The financial authorities should try to boost investor confidence in the securities market by better regulating the industry, Mi said, adding that development of secure investment funds should be accelerated.
The high savings rate had helped to prop up state banks, which are saddled with huge bad debts to state-owned enterprises, Mi said.
"The major banks cannot survive without the high savings deposits," Mi said, but did not elaborate.
The central bank in May lowered interest rates on deposits by an average 0.98 percentage points and followed that in August with another cut of 1.5 percentage points.
